prompt: You boot your Kali VM for a new exercise and run `ping -c 3 8.8.8.8`. Which result actually confirms your lab is still isolated from the internet?
choices: The ping succeeds with low latency
The ping fails immediately with 'Network is unreachable'
The ping times out with no response after a long wait
The ping resolves the hostname but gets no reply

prompt: Inside your Kali VM, `docker ps` shows Juice Shop bound to 0.0.0.0:3000->3000/tcp. Why is this binding currently safe?
choices: 0.0.0.0 bindings are never reachable from outside the container by design
Docker automatically firewalls port 3000 unless you open it explicitly
Kali's VM currently has only one network interface, on the isolated host-only subnet with no route out, so 0.0.0.0 is only reachable through that one path
Juice Shop requires a login before any network traffic reaches it, regardless of binding

prompt: You run `VBoxManage showvminfo "kali-linux" --machinereadable | grep -i nic` on your host machine and see nic2="nat". What does this mean right now?
choices: Nothing — nic2 only matters if something inside the guest OS is actively using it
A second network adapter is live at the hypervisor level with NAT (internet-reaching) access, regardless of what the guest OS currently shows
This is the expected, safe default configuration for a host-only lab
It only affects outbound traffic from the host machine, not the VM

prompt: In the example Rules of Engagement document, the IN SCOPE entry for Juice Shop is written as '192.168.56.101:3000', not just 'Juice Shop'. Why does that specificity matter?
choices: IP:port notation is required by the CFAA for any authorization document
'Juice Shop' alone could be misread as covering the publicly hosted demo instance other people run on the internet, which is not yours to test
Docker containers change their name randomly on every restart
It has no real effect; it's just a stylistic convention

prompt: From a second device on your real home Wi-Fi (not your host machine, not the VM), you run `nmap -sn 192.168.56.0/24`. What result confirms correct host-only isolation?
choices: The scan finds your Kali VM at 192.168.56.101
The scan reports 0 hosts up on that subnet
The scan times out entirely and produces no report
The scan reports your home router as the only live host

prompt: Why does this module have you re-read your Rules of Engagement document before every exercise, rather than just once after writing it?
choices: Legal documents expire automatically after 30 days
Re-reading triggers a required Docker container restart
The habit of checking scope before acting is the actual skill being built, and skipped habits decay even when the underlying document hasn't changed
PortSwigger requires proof of a recent ROE review before granting lab access

prompt: Running `ip route` inside your Kali VM shows only: '192.168.56.0/24 dev eth0 proto kernel scope link src 192.168.56.101'. What should you conclude?
choices: There is no default route out of the VM — traffic can only reach the host-only subnet
The VM has no network connectivity at all, including to Juice Shop and DVWA
A default route exists but is hidden from this command
This output indicates a misconfigured bridged adapter

prompt: Which of these would correctly belong in the OUT OF SCOPE section of a personal lab's Rules of Engagement document?
choices: Your own DVWA container running on your isolated Kali VM
PortSwigger Web Security Academy's hosted practice labs
A publicly hosted Juice Shop demo instance run by someone else on the internet
Your own Juice Shop container reachable at 192.168.56.101:3000
